principles: Receipt-backed Authority is stronger than local lifecycle evidence only when a signed receipt is actually verified.
Fail-closed is a valid and useful result for strong-evidence readiness validation.
Do not optimize or redesign Authority flow while validating current capability.
Keep host-neutral and local/Authority boundaries mechanically visible.
drivers: User wants to see actual strong-evidence flow and evidence result.
Existing docs forbid thin CLI local evidence from becoming L2+ Authority evidence.
The environment may not have Authority Server credentials or server key material.

options.name: A: Real Authority attempt with fail-closed report
pros: Produces clear receipt-backed or blocked evidence
cons: May finish as blocked if server credentials are missing

options.name: B: Simulate a receipt locally
cons: Would violate Authority trust boundary and could mislead gate consumers

options.name: C: Only document the future flow
cons: Does not answer the user request to verify the current flow and evidence result

chosen: A: Real Authority attempt with fail-closed report
rationale: Option A is the only path that both attempts real strong evidence and preserves correctness if the server path is unavailable.

preMortem.consequence: No server-backed job or receipt can be produced
preMortem.mitigation: Record BLOCKED fail-closed report with receiptVerified=false and next actions.

preMortem.scenario: Authority Server accepts job but no receipt can be fetched or verified
preMortem.trigger: job_create succeeds but receipt_fetch/verify fails or server public key is absent
preMortem.consequence: Evidence is not strong enough for Authority gate consumption
preMortem.mitigation: Record jobId separately from verifiedReceipt and keep productionDone=false.

preMortem.trigger: report sets authorityMode=enforce or receiptVerified=true without verified receipt
preMortem.consequence: False strong-evidence claim breaks trust boundary
preMortem.mitigation: Mechanical check fails unless receipt verification output proves the claim.
